title: refactor(terraform/private): unify state layout & modules for GPU node pools, IAM, networking
author: Marina Patel
release_notes: Unifies Terraform state layout for private deployments and introduces consolidated modules for GPU node pools, IAM roles, and VPC networking. Existing Private customers must follow the documented migration steps. Backwards-incompatible state layout changes require a one-time migration and operator coordination.
description: Motivation: Private deployments have accumulated multiple ad-hoc Terraform state layouts and duplicated module logic across clusters (gpu node pools, IAM roles, and networking). This PR refactors and consolidates those into a small set of validated, versioned modules and a unified state layout to simplify upgrades, reduce drift, and enable safer automated upgrades for on-prem/VPC installs. Summary of changes: - Introduces modules/private/state-layout.tf which standardizes workspace and state key naming for customer environments. - Adds modules/gpu-node-pool: unified node pool module with consistent labels, taints, autoscaling, and GPU accelerator handling across GKE/AKS/EKS. - Adds modules/iam: centralizes service account, role, and policy attachments; supports customer-managed KMS bindings. - Adds modules/network: consistent VPC/subnet, peering, and firewall rules to match Private install expectations. - Migration tooling: examples/private/upgrade-migration.md and a terraform helper script tools/tf-state-migrate.sh that automates the state move for common layouts. - Tests: terraform unit inputs + local e2e smoke harness for Private installer using KinD + mocked cloud providers. Migration notes (operator-facing): This PR changes the expected terraform state keys and moves resources into the consolidated modules. Operators must: 1) Read examples/private/upgrade-migration.md and run the pre-checks. 2) Run tools/tf-state-migrate.sh in a staging environment to validate mappings. 3) Coordinate a short maintenance window; migration is best-effort but may require manual state edits for unusual customizations. Rollback strategy: - If the migration fails, revert to the pre-migration state backups (the helper script creates a dated backup) and re-apply the previous module set. - For partial migrations, the helper will create a plan to move remaining resources and an undo plan. CI and validation: - terraform validate and tflint run on modules. - terraform plan smoke for each cloud target (GKE/EKS/AKS) in CI. - e2e private-installer smoke tests (dockerized) were run and passing after two fixes (see commits). Backwards compatibility: This PR is a breaking change for on-prem terraform state only; runtime behavior is unchanged. We added feature flags (module_version pinning) to allow a staged rollout. Related: ENG-2482 (migration epic), INFRA-732 (private installer stability). Checklist: - [x] Extract modules and move implementation - [x] Add migration docs and helper script - [x] Add unit and smoke tests - [x] Get infra and platform review - [x] Run staged migration in internal environment Commits (high level): - init: extract private state layout module - feat(modules/gpu): unified gpu node pool module + autoscaler support - feat(modules/iam): consolidate roles and service accounts - feat(modules/network): vpc/subnet/peering module - docs: add migration guide + examples - ci: add plan checks for gke/eks/aks - fix: address race in state-migrate helper - tests: add e2e smoke harness Results: After review and two CI reruns to stabilize plan checks the PR was approved by reviewers and merged with squash. See CI checks and review thread below for details.
